summary: This sermon concludes a four-week series on Sabbath by arguing that the goal of Sabbath practice is worship—defined as growing in surrender to God. While stopping, resting, and delighting are essential practices, they must lead us to recognize God as the giver of all good gifts, not become ends in themselves.
key_points: Sabbath is made 'holy'—set apart for the Lord, not just for moral goodness
Worship means surrender: receiving God's gifts and giving them back with open hands
We can practice Sabbath wrongly by enjoying the gifts without growing in surrender to the giver
God's beauty and pleasure are both gift and map, leading us back to Him
Sabbath forms a counter-community with different loyalties in a work-obsessed culture
big_idea: Sabbath is a day set apart for God where we grow in surrender to Him through experiencing Him as the source of every good gift.
title: PTW Sabbath: WORSHP
